fairness_notes: Both solvers single-threaded: Fortran starter/engine with -np 1 -nt 1 (OMP_NUM_THREADS=1), pyradioss as one NumPy process (default thread env untouched by harness; CLI -nt not passed).

starter_s/engine_s are subprocess WALL CLOCKS measured around each call (includes process startup: ~1s Python interpreter+imports for the port, binary load for Fortran); *_self_s are the solvers' own reported ELAPSED TIME from their .out listings (exclude startup).
Same machine as perf_m36.json; background load uncontrolled (desktop system).

n_cycles differs per solver on the same deck (independent time-step evolution), so cycles_per_s is a per-solver throughput, not a same-work ratio; elements_x_cycles_per_s is the fairer cross-solver rate.
Fortran anim/T01 output frequency follows the deck; the port writes T01 as CSV directly (no th_to_csv step in its timing).

Official-suite case ids c00..c39 are identical to perf_m36.json (same inventory-order naming); c40+ are the packages M37 plausibly unlocked (RD-E-1000 BT, RD-V-0220 LAW70 foam, RD-V-0230 LAW19 fabric).
SKIPPED-SLOW rows carry the PARTIAL timings measured up to the 900 s port budget, not a completed run.

CPU CONTENTION: records carrying a 'contention_note' field (all bundled-suite records + official cases finished after 2026-07-17 00:35 local) ran concurrently with the user's 13-process MPI simulation (getriebekette) on this machine; their wall clocks are UPPER BOUNDS, not clean measurements. Cycle counts and parity classes are unaffected. The bundled sweep additionally overlapped the tail of the official sweep (two single-threaded jobs). Official cases finished before 00:35 (c26,c10,c11,c15,c21,c22,c17,c24,c13,c14,c19,c20,c12,c18,c01,c02,c03,c04,c08,c09,c40,c41,c42,c43) are clean.
